question: Does Sonnet 5.5 solve pk-prerel cleanly without the advisor too? cand-1 gave 3/3 clean A runs on wzf-cond and on pk-prerel, all with the voluntary Opus advisor available and used (1-3 calls per run). If A0 also passes 3/3, the advisor is not what makes these tasks easy (ChatGPT, 21.11, option 2).
not_asked: The causal effect of the advisor. The three earlier A runs on pk-prerel are a historical reference only; comparing them with new A0 runs proves nothing causal.

task.hidden_tests: as in cand-1 (62511 on the Mac, 28 bug_tests)

mode.A0: Sonnet 5.5, effort high, no advisor (no --advisor; an advisor call or any Opus use makes the run invalid); rules and Jev only record (observe)

counted_outcomes: exactly three. A budget timeout (timeout_class budget) is a failure and counts.
replacement: only an attempt invalid for an infrastructure reason is replaced: api_interrupted (e.g. a rejected subscription rate limit), timeout_class infra_suspected, or an operator_reported failure under the cand-1 rule (source, interval, affected runs, reason; applied alike to successes and failures). A replacement runs in a new batch with seed 711, then 721. Any other invalid attempt (e.g. an advisor or Opus call in A0, a cost or integrity problem) stops the pilot for review instead of being replaced.
recorded_per_run: run_usd and run_usd_status (whole run, confirmed or not)

decision_after.A0 3/3 clean: go to cand-1 option (1): larger cross-cutting tasks (migrations across several subsystems with checkable invariants)
decision_after.A0 fails or regresses at least once: test the effect of the advisor being available in a separate fresh paired A/A0 series with the order shuffled within pairs, declared apart; pk-prerel stays 'not selected' for improving the outcome over A - the cand-1 criterion is not changed after the fact
